supersedes: zcash-nu7-questions-v2.json (v2, markets created 2026-09-09, fully unwound the same day, left live and abandoned)
snapshotOf: Google Doc as read 2026-09-09, after the v2 snapshot — re-read and diffed against v2: the ballot is UNCHANGED (same 5 questions, same options, same base rates, same 3 general notes). v3 is a rename-only rebuild.
baseRatesFrom: the 'Base Rate' column of the source doc, taken verbatim; each question's rates sum to 1.000
marketType: categorical (single-select) — MarketFactory.createCategoricalMarket, REALITY_SINGLE_SELECT_TEMPLATE. The options within each question are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so exactly one wins and price == P(that option). NOT multi-categorical (which normalises payouts across k winners) and NOT multi-scalar (which prices vote share).
changesFromV2: Market names only. v2 appended the full resolution rules to every marketName, which made them unreadably long; v3 names carry the question and nothing else. Outcomes, tags, seed prices, market type and openingTime are identical to v2.
resolutionRules: The winning option as revealed on 2026-09-15 resolves to 1; all other options resolve to 0.
Abstain is not an outcome in these markets. If Abstain is the highest-voted option in the official poll, the second highest-voted option counts as the winner.
If a question does not reach the official quorum requirements, the market reverts — i.e. resolves Invalid.
resolutionRulesPlacement: OFF-CHAIN, by explicit decision on 2026-09-09. Unlike v2, these rules are NOT written into the question text — they live only in this file and in the source doc. Reality resolves off the question text alone, so rules 2 and 3 are convention, not something a resolver is bound by. See hazard 'unrecorded rules'.
note: price is the seeded pool price for each outcome. tag drives the wrapped ERC20 symbol ZNU7V3<shortName><tag> and must be unique within a question. 'Invalid result' is appended by the factory: it is not listed here, gets no tokenName, and gets no pool.
hazard: Invalid is a live outcome here, not a tail: doc rule 3 sends a below-quorum question straight to Invalid, and Invalid is deliberately unpooled. Whoever learns of a quorum failure first buys Invalid at ~0 and takes the pool. In v3 that rule is no longer stated on-chain, so the market text gives a resolver no basis for it at all.
